harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured daily log rotation for /var/log/inventory/app.log on node1 via /etc/logrotate.d/inventory (daily, rotate 7, compress, copytruncate, missingok, notifempty). Verified the config parses cleanly, is picked up by the active systemd logrotate.timer, and that two forced rotations correctly aged/compressed rotations (app.log.1.gz, app.log.2.gz) while the application file remained writable after each rotation (copytruncate preserves the fd since no PID/service exists to signal). Completed the mandatory single-node restart protocol: captured boot_id baseline, issued a non-blocking systemctl reboot, polled until the node returned with a new boot_id, and confirmed the logrotate config, timer, and prior rotated archives all survived the reboot, with the app log still writable and rotation logic still correctly tracking the last-rotated timestamp.
actions_performed: Inspected /var/log/inventory/app.log and confirmed no running service/PID owns it (simulated app log)
Checked available logrotate.d configs and global logrotate.conf for repo conventions
Wrote /etc/logrotate.d/inventory with daily, rotate 7, compress, copytruncate, missingok, notifempty
Validated config with `logrotate -d` (dry run) — no errors
Confirmed systemd logrotate.timer is active/enabled for daily execution
Forced two rotations (`logrotate -f`) to prove compression, correct rotation numbering/retention, and that the app log remained writable (copytruncate) both before and after rotation
Captured pre-restart boot_id baseline and healthy state (timer active, config present, rotations present)
Issued a non-blocking `systemctl reboot` on node1 that let the acknowledgement return before disconnecting
Polled node1 until exec succeeded again
Verified boot_id changed (d052eb57... -> 59d5b29e...), confirming an actual reboot
Post-reboot: verified logrotate.timer active, config persisted, previous compressed rotations intact, app log still writable, and logrotate status tracking correct

evidence.requirement: Daily rotation with 7 compressed rotations kept, app can continue writing after rotation
evidence.summary: Created /etc/logrotate.d/inventory (daily, rotate 7, compress, copytruncate); dry-run validated; two forced rotations produced app.log.1.gz and app.log.2.gz while app.log remained writable and correctly received new writes immediately after each rotation

evidence.requirement: Daily execution mechanism is active on the node
evidence.summary: systemctl status/list-timers show logrotate.timer is loaded, enabled, and active (waiting), scheduled to fire daily
Captured boot_id d052eb57-c81d-4309-ae7f-bce362073ff9, confirmed logrotate.timer active and rotation files/config present
Backgrounded systemctl reboot returned acknowledgement immediately; subsequent polls timed out/reset while node was down; later poll succeeded again

evidence.requirement: node1 changed boot identity proving actual restart
evidence.summary: Post-reboot boot_id is 59d5b29e-86ec-4dbe-a7bd-818f80560872, different from the pre-reboot boot_id, and uptime -s shows a fresh boot time

evidence.requirement: node1 post-restart recovery of required config/service and data
evidence.summary: After reboot, logrotate.timer active, /etc/logrotate.d/inventory config intact, previously rotated compressed logs (app.log.1.gz, app.log.2.gz) preserved, app.log still writable, and logrotate correctly reports the log was already rotated within the last day
